text:
alex: quick thought — proposing we add a namespaced shared-KV cache entry as part of model ingest metadata to avoid cold-start penalties during admit checks. idea: each model gets a `kv_namespace` and a `compat_hash`, TTL configurable.

maria: hmm, sharing cache between variants worries me for Private customers (data isolation). are we sure namespacing + kms is enough? :thinking:

sam: namespacing + strict RBAC and envelope encryption should cover it. we can require `tenant_id` in the ingest contract for private deployments and refuse shared cache for tenant-scoped models.

jordan: operationally this helps a lot. current bench runs warm up a lot of shards. if ingest writes a small canonical prefix (like embedding of prompt templates + tokenizer state) we can reduce the warm path by ~30%. we should add regression tests that verify warmup latency < X ms.

alex: agreed. draft ingest snippet i've been thinking about:
```yaml
ingest_metadata:
  model_id: "llama-4x-quantized"
  compat_hash: "sha256:af3e..."
  kv_namespace: "ingest/v3/llama-4x-quant"
  cache_ttl_seconds: 7200
  tenant_id: null # required for private deployments
  allowed_cache_sharing: false
```

devon: small nit — add `fallback_policy` to the contract so runtime can evict to a cheaper variant if the shared cache is unavailable. otherwise callers get hot fails.

katie: +1 on fallback. also we need a compatibility check that validates `compat_hash` meaningfully. suggest we run a deterministic `smoke_input_set` and store an output fingerprint; any runtime serving variant must match fingerprint within tolerances. that should be part of the gating step.

alex: yes — two separate signals: `compat_hash` for binary/shape compatibility and `behavior_fingerprint` for output drift. the gating pipeline should run both. if fingerprint mismatch > threshold -> fail and open a manual review.

maria: for private deploys, make `allowed_cache_sharing` default to false and require override in infra config with org-approved audit trail.

sam: CI action idea: `ci-bot` runs a small-scale smoke using the ingest metadata when PR to model-registry is created. if `cache_ttl_seconds` > 0 and `allowed_cache_sharing` is true, CI must run an additional isolation test.

ci-bot: ran smoke: 2164001300 - warmup delta 28% reduced, behavior_fingerprint diff 0.002 (within threshold).

jordan: can we store the `behavior_fingerprint` in the model registry and surface it in Console? would help SRE when investigating regressions.

alex: yes — metadata fields: `compat_hash`, `behavior_fingerprint`, `kv_namespace`, `fallback_policy`, `allowed_cache_sharing`, `tenant_id`. Add Console panel to show last-smoke timestamp and CI run link.

devon: one more tradeoff — cache invalidation. if we auto-evict on rollout, we might spike tokens on the first N requests. propose a gradual priming job that pro-actively populates caches in background across shards. add priming job id to ingest metadata.

katie: and a cost calc in the ingest UI showing estimated priming tokens and estimated warm savings over first 24h. PLG users will want transparency.

alex: awesome. i'll open a short follow-up RFC with the ingest contract schema + CI checks + Console surface tomorrow. tagging @maria @sam for the private deploy constraints and @devon for priming job design. :thumbsup:
